svg.title: HQ Campus — OSPF Area 10: detailed topology (healthy baseline)
svg.desc: Detailed HQ Campus topology from the Cisco CML lab: every routed /31 link with interfaces, addresses and OSPF cost; LACP port-channels and members; HSRP active and STP root roles per distribution switch; hq-a1 access ports and VLANs; the management path from the CML external connector; and a VLAN and gateway table.
svg.text: Cisco CML · OSPF process 10 · 5 devices + external connector · 19 links (L0–L18) · 10 × P2P /31 · 3 LACP port-channels · 10 VLANs
Planned uplinks from hq-r1 and hq-r2 · not built
CML L0, L1 · Root Guard on hq-d1
CML L2, L3 · Root Guard on hq-d2
Edge ports: PortFast edge + BPDU Guard · Gi2/0 also carries voice VLAN 120 (VOICE)
Unused ports: Gi0/2-3, Gi1/2-3 in PARKING 191, shutdown
HSRP active and STP root as configured for the healthy baseline
HSRP: the active gateway runs priority 110 with preempt; the standby peer keeps the default 100.
Rapid PVST+: root priority 24576, peer 28672. hq-a1 forwards each VLAN on the uplink towards its root; the other uplink is the STP alternate.
Trunks Po10, Po20 and Po30: 802.1Q, native VLAN 190, allowed 112, 120, 130, 140, 152, 160, 170, 190, 199. PARKING 191 is not trunked.
Management return: hq-r2, hq-d1 and hq-d2 route 192.0.2.10/32 via 10.255.10.129 (hq-r1 Lo0); hq-a1 uses its default gateway 10.10.99.1.
Source: CML topology and device configurations · Phase 10 healthy baseline
